candidate.title: TruSeq™ RNA Exome
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq RNA Exome enrichment route depicted in the assigned Illumina footer schematic: pooling prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries, hybridizing biotinylated target probes, capturing probe-associated library on streptavidin magnetic beads, and eluting a product ready for cluster generation. RNA-to-library preparation and cluster generation/sequencing are outside the depicted transformations. No kit revision, alternative workflow or primary-paper association is supplied.

states.label: Prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries before pooling
features: Already prepared libraries are the starting material; native RNA conversion is not drawn.

The biological target is RNA-derived sequence represented in the prepared library. Interpretation: the P5/P7-indexed, cluster-ready carrier is a DNA/cDNA sequencing library; the figure itself does not explicitly label DNA or depict its synthesis.
Target-bearing library fragments and differently colored terminal segments are shown. No cells or intact compartments are depicted.

evidence.locator: Upper library-fragment bundle and caption 'Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries'
evidence.rationale: The explicit pooling instruction presupposes prepared libraries as inputs. A separate pre-pooling panel is not drawn.

evidence.locator: Stranded RNA-Seq library input followed by retained target fragment ending as P5/Index 2/Target/Index 1/P7 product ready for cluster generation
evidence.rationale: The explicit library designation and Illumina cluster-generation interface identify a prepared sequencing-library carrier of RNA-derived sequence. Interpreting that carrier as DNA/cDNA distinguishes the selected library from native RNA without adding an unshown reverse-transcription operation or a strand-synthesis mechanism.

states.label: Pool of stranded RNA-Seq libraries containing target fragments
features: Multiple fragments form a common pool of the already prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries; the upper highlighted fragment has a region labeled Target.
The colored terminal architecture is carried through capture and elution; the final drawing identifies P5, Index 2, Index 1 and P7.

evidence.locator: Upper Target-labeled fragments and pooling caption

states.label: Biotinylated target probe
features: Short blue probe with an attached biotin marker, identified by the caption.
Probe nucleic-acid chemistry and which end carries biotin are not specified.

evidence.locator: Plus sign, short blue probe with pendant marker, and 'Biotinylated target probe' caption

states.label: Library target hybridized to biotinylated probe
features: The long library fragment remains intact while the short probe is paired beneath its target region.
Biotin is carried by the probe associated with the target, rather than being depicted as a covalent modification of the library fragment.

evidence.locator: Middle paired long target and short biotin-marked probe under 'Hybridize probes to targets'

states.label: Streptavidin magnetic beads
features: Capture reagent named by the bead-capture caption; the grey bead surface bears blue capture icons.
Beads serve as an attachment support and are retained in the captured complex, rather than being transformed into library sequence.

evidence.locator: Grey bead surface with blue icons and 'Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads'

states.label: Bead-attached probe–library target complex
features: Probe-hybridized library target is tethered to the streptavidin bead surface through the probe's biotin association.
The target-bearing fragment and its colored terminal segments remain present; the changed state is bead attachment.

evidence.locator: Capture panel: target/probe above bead surface with contact through pendant probe marker

states.label: Eluted target-enriched library ready for cluster generation
features: A free library fragment is shown without the bead or short capture probe.
Final labels run left to right: P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, P7. No 5′/3′ polarity, UMI or cell barcode is labeled.

The readout carrier is the retained RNA-derived library target sequence. Index segments provide library-identification information; no sequence data or quantitative expression measurement is generated in this panel.

evidence.locator: Elute arrow and final P5–Index 2–Target–Index 1–P7 product, 'Product ready for cluster generation'

evidence.rationale: Following the target-bearing RNA-Seq library through capture to a cluster-ready product identifies the library insert as the biological-sequence carrier and the labeled indices as library-identification segments. Sequencing itself is not shown.

operations.label: Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries
operations.description: Combine already prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries into the pool that receives target probes. The substrate changes from separate prepared libraries to a shared library mixture; no RNA conversion or new adapter/index construction is depicted.
operations.mechanism: Pooling of library material, as explicitly captioned.
operations.information_effect: Library target sequences enter a common mixture. The drawing retains colored terminal segments through the route and labels two index regions in the final product; index addition is not a depicted operation.

evidence.locator: Upper library bundle and 'Pool stranded RNA-Seq libraries' caption

operations.label: Hybridize probes to targets
operations.description: Add the biotinylated target probes to the library pool, as indicated by the plus sign, and associate probes with library target regions. The output is a target–probe hybrid with a biotin capture handle; the target-bearing library fragment is retained.
operations.mechanism: Sequence-directed probe–target hybridization, shown by the short probe aligned beneath the long fragment's target region.
operations.information_effect: Probe complementarity links a library target to a biotin-bearing capture reagent. The physical readout carrier remains the RNA-derived library fragment; the probe supplies the capture association and is not drawn as a replacement readout molecule.

evidence.locator: Library + biotinylated probe, downward arrow, and 'Hybridize probes to targets' panel

operations.label: Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads
operations.description: Attach the biotinylated probe-associated library target to streptavidin magnetic beads. A soluble target–probe hybrid becomes bead-associated while retaining the library fragment and its terminal segments.
operations.mechanism: Biotin on the hybridized probe mediates association with bead-associated streptavidin, as indicated by the named reagents and the drawn tether.
operations.information_effect: Retention is mediated by probe association, enriching library fragments recognized by the target probes. The selected sequence content therefore depends on the probe targets and the material already present in the input libraries. The single retained target is illustrative; the drawing establishes neither exhaustive target recovery nor perfect exclusion of other fragments. No separate discarded-material branch is drawn.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from target–probe hybrid to bead-tethered target; bead-capture caption
Target-probe hybridization followed by capture of the probe-associated library fragment
evidence.rationale: Because attachment is mediated by a target probe binding pre-existing library sequence, the retained population represents the probe-accessible subset of that library. This schematic selection route does not measure recovery, off-target retention or transcript abundance.

operations.label: Elute
operations.description: Release the captured target-bearing library from the bead-associated capture complex. The depicted output is a free target-containing fragment retaining both index regions and the P5/P7 terminal architecture, ready for cluster generation.
operations.mechanism: Elution is captioned; the drawing does not specify the chemistry that releases the library.
operations.information_effect: The selected library target sequence and index architecture remain in the sequencing-compatible product. Bead attachment is removed; the capture probe is absent from the final depiction. Subsequent sequencing could read library target and index information, but no sequencing or analysis operation is shown.

The supplied sources contain no primary publication or required paper association, so empty paper_matches is appropriate. No consequential source conflict, correction, or architecture-changing unknown is established.
